title: Best ChatGPT Plugins for Students: Understand, Practice and Review
summary: One biology question run through ChatGPT's plugin directory on 8 September 2026. Which study plugins earned their install, and the job that needed none.
body_markdown:
Studying inside ChatGPT is three separate jobs, and they do not want the same tool. Getting a concept to land is one. Practicing until you can reproduce it is another. Reviewing it three weeks later, when the exam is real, is a third. On the runs recorded for this article, one of those three jobs needed no plugin at all. The task was one biology question put through ChatGPT's plugin directory on 8 September 2026, once with nothing installed and once with a plugin installed. Both outcomes are below, including the one where nothing happened.


> Scrimba publishes this article and makes one of the plugins in it. Scrimba Explain, listed in the directory as **Explain Video Generator** , appears in the first of the three jobs beside a competitor described at the same length, and does not compete in the third job at all. For the video-plugin roundup rather than the student one,[that comparison](https://scrimba.com/articles/best-chatgpt-plugins-for-creating-videos-2026/) covers it.


## One Study Task, Four Runs


The task was the kind of thing a student actually types: explain how photosynthesis converts light into sugar, for a first-year biology student. Then a follow-up asking to be tested on it.


Photosynthesis was not chosen to flatter anyone. It is what these listings use to sell themselves. Quizlet's first example card in the plugin directory reads *Create flashcards on photosynthesis* , and Wayground offers *create flashcards on photosynthesis for grade 5* , both read signed out on 8 September 2026. Running them on their own showcase topic removes any excuse that the task was unfair.


The baseline came first: the question with no plugin involved at all.


It answered, and answered well. Everything below is measured against that paragraph. Each condition ran once, so every number describes one output rather than a promised format.


## Nothing Happens Until the Plugin Is Installed


Start with the failure, the one most readers meet first.


Signed out, with nothing installed, the same question went in with an @ mention of the plugin in front of it. ChatGPT answered in ordinary prose, near enough identical to the baseline. The mention was read as the everyday word it happens to be.


No error, no greyed-out control, nothing saying a plugin had been skipped. That silence is the problem. A student follows advice that says to type a plugin name, gets a good answer, and concludes the plugin is either fake or already working. Neither is true.


OpenAI is direct about the conditions sitting between a reader and a working plugin:


> The Plugins Directory is visible across ChatGPT plans. Whether you can install or invoke a plugin depends on your plan, workspace settings, role, supported surface, region, and the capabilities of its included apps.


Be precise about what those two runs prove. One was signed out with nothing installed, the other signed in with the plugin installed. They establish that installation changes the outcome, and nothing about which ChatGPT plan you need.


The route is short and OpenAI publishes it: go to **Plugins** , select the plugin and review its included apps, select **Install plugin** , then select **Connect** if an app asks for account authorization. After that you call it with an @ mention, or by opening **+** and selecting **More** . Scrimba's companion walkthrough,[How to Install and Use a ChatGPT Plugin](https://scrimba.com/articles/how-to-install-a-plugin-in-chatgpt-2026/) , records the route with screenshots.


One case catches students specifically. On a school account, administrators manage installation in **Workspace settings > Plugins** , and new Enterprise and Edu workspaces start with a selected set of apps enabled rather than everything. A dead install control on a university login is usually policy, not a fault.


## Understand: Getting the Concept to Land


ChatGPT already does this job unaided. The baseline answer laid out the light reactions and the Calvin cycle in readable order, and plain text beats every alternative here at skimming, pasting into notes, and finding a line again a week later. A plugin has to beat that, not merely differ from it.


**ELI5** makes the visual argument. Its tagline is *Picture-first HTML explainers* , and its listing describes turning a difficult topic into a beginner-friendly explainer of large diagrams, plain language and progressive steps, saved as one portable file. For a mechanism with stages and arrows, that shape fits.


Its limits sit on the same page, to its credit. It is skills-only, with no MCP server, no hosted backend and no account system, so nothing is stored for you. Its directory category is Productivity rather than Education, the developer field names an individual rather than a company, and version 0.2.6 is early software.


**Scrimba Explain** , listed as **Explain Video Generator** , makes the other argument: watch it instead of reading it. Signed in with the plugin installed, naming the plugin ahead of the same question produced a status line and then a card rather than a paragraph.


The status line read *Worked for 2m 2s* . What came back was titled "Photosynthesis: Light to Sugar", marked 13 slides and 3 min, with a diagram tracing light through the thylakoid to ATP and NADPH and on to the Calvin cycle, and a control to watch the explainer inline. That is one generation, so the runtime and slide count describe that output and not a fixed format. It is free during its open beta, and that is all that is known about the cost.


Its limits deserve the same space. It explains a question against real context rather than generating video from an arbitrary prompt, so it is not a text-to-video model. It does no avatars, stock footage or brand templates, so it is not a marketing video tool. Scrimba's own FAQ says it can make mistakes and anything important should be double-checked. And it produces no flashcards and schedules no reviews, which matters below. The[full product guide](https://scrimba.com/articles/how-to-use-scrimba-explain/) covers the other ways to reach it.


When to skip both: a three-minute video is slower to search than a paragraph. Half-understanding the material and needing one step clarified is a job for the plain answer.


## Practice: The Job That Needs No Plugin


This is the section that should sell you something and does not.


Asked to produce three questions checking whether the explanation had landed, plain ChatGPT produced three real ones, one of them asking the reader to transfer the idea rather than repeat it back.


The same follow-up typed inside the plugin thread also returned three questions, and on that particular run they were sharper: the two stages and where each happens, the roles of water, light, ATP, NADPH and oxygen, and why the Calvin cycle does not directly produce glucose.


That difference is worth one sentence, because it is one run against one run. It is not a benchmark, and nobody should install anything on the strength of it.


What was asked Plugin involved What came back


Explain how photosynthesis converts light into sugar None A long structured prose answer


The same question, with an @ mention, signed out None fired Near-identical prose. No error, no indication anything was skipped


The same question, plugin installed and signed in Explain Video Generator *Worked for 2m 2s* , then a card: 13 slides, 3 min, a diagram, a watch control


Ask me three questions to check I understood None Three comprehension questions, including one that transfers the idea


ChatGPT also ships a study feature that needs no install. Announcing study mode on 29 July 2025, OpenAI described guiding questions rather than answers, scaffolded responses, and knowledge checks it defined as quizzes and open-ended questions with personalized feedback. That announcement stated availability for logged-in users on Free, Plus, Pro and Team, with ChatGPT Edu to follow. Treat it as the position at that date.


One practice case does need a plugin. **Wayground** , published by Quizizz Inc., turns your own instructional material into ready-to-assign quizzes and study cards and reports on how learners engaged with them. For a teacher setting practice for thirty people, that reporting is real value. Its limit follows from the same design: activities are delivered through Wayground, so the practice happens outside the chat, and the product is built around assigning rather than self-testing.


For a student testing themselves, the verdict is plain. To be quizzed on what you just read, a plugin is a detour.


## Review: Where a Plugin Earns Its Place


Review is where the argument for installing something gets strong.


Understanding decays on a schedule. A chat thread does not come back on Thursday to ask whether you still know it, and neither does a video. A deck does. That is a scheduling problem rather than a content problem, and the one job here ChatGPT cannot do by itself.


**Quizlet** is the direct route. Its plugin creates flashcards from any prompt or file, handles the formatting, and builds a set from notes you paste in rather than making you retype them. Published by Quizlet under Education and Research, version 4.0.0. Its limit is structural: making cards is not reviewing them. Generation happens in the chat, studying happens in Quizlet.


**Recall** goes further into the mechanism. Its listing describes creating spaced repetition decks from ChatGPT, writing atomic cards that follow memory-retention principles, scheduling them so review starts immediately, and surfacing the cards you keep missing. One of its example prompts is *Which words am I struggling with in Japanese?* , the right question for this job. The caveat applies twice over: another account, another app, and a schedule only helps if you open it.


Scrimba Explain does not compete here, and that is worth saying rather than leaving a gap. It makes no flashcards and schedules no reviews. If review is the job in front of you, install one of the other two.


One warning covers all of them. Cards generated from a conversation inherit that conversation's mistakes, and a wrong card on a spaced schedule is a wrong fact rehearsed to permanence. Check the cards against the course material once before the schedule starts. For study tools outside ChatGPT entirely,[the wider roundup](https://scrimba.com/articles/best-ai-study-tools-2026/) covers that ground.


## The Three Jobs, Side by Side


Job What actually helps Needs a plugin? Options in the directory


Understand A second explanation in a different shape: a diagram, or something to watch No, but a plugin can genuinely change the format ELI5, Explain Video Generator


Practice Being asked questions you cannot answer by pattern-matching No. ChatGPT does this unprompted, and study mode formalizes it Wayground, for assigning practice to a group


Review Cards that come back on a schedule weeks later Yes. This is the job the chat cannot do Quizlet, Recall


Read down the middle column: the further a job sits from the conversation you are already having, the more a plugin is worth installing.


## What a Study Plugin Cannot Do for You


A short list, because the listings do not lead with it.


Every connected plugin carries the same data notice: ChatGPT may share relevant chats and memories with the app to give it context, and the vendor's use of that data falls under the vendor's own terms and privacy policy. For coursework that is unremarkable. For anything under an academic confidentiality rule it is worth reading once rather than never.


The directory does not show prices. Whatever these tools cost is set on the vendor's side, so a ChatGPT subscription buys none of it, and this article states no price for any of them.


None publishes an accuracy guarantee, so the check runs against your course material rather than against the tool that produced the answer. And the plugins to be careful with are the ones that hand over a finished artifact, since a set of cards you did not read is a set of cards you have not learned. For where these tools help and where they quietly hurt,[AI tutors](https://scrimba.com/articles/ai-tutors-what-they-do-well/) covers the argument. If your subject is programming,[AI tools and courses for learning to code](https://scrimba.com/articles/best-ai-tools-and-courses-for-learning-to-code/) is the narrower guide.


## Which One Should a Student Install First?


- **Testing yourself on something you just read.** Install nothing. Ask ChatGPT for three questions and answer them without scrolling up.
- **You want to be walked through it rather than told.** Study mode, also nothing to install.
- **The material has not landed after two readings.** An explainer plugin: ELI5 for a diagram page you keep, Explain Video Generator to watch it instead.
- **An exam is weeks away.** A card plugin: Quizlet if you already live there, Recall if you want the scheduling done for you.
- **You are setting practice for a class.** Wayground, for the assigning and the reporting.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### What are the best ChatGPT plugins for students?


It depends which of three jobs you have. For understanding a concept in a different format, ELI5 builds a diagram-first explainer page and Explain Video Generator returns a narrated video. For reviewing weeks later, Quizlet and Recall build flashcard decks, and Recall schedules them. For practicing right now, no plugin is needed.


### Do you need a plugin to quiz yourself in ChatGPT?


No. Asked to produce three questions checking comprehension, plain ChatGPT produced three real ones, including a question that required transferring the idea rather than repeating it. ChatGPT also has a built-in study mode that runs knowledge checks. Installing a plugin to be quizzed on material already in the conversation is a detour.


### Why did nothing happen when I typed a plugin name in ChatGPT?


Almost always because the plugin is not installed on the account you are using. Signed out with nothing installed, an at-mention of a plugin returned ordinary prose with no error and no warning. Install it from the plugin directory first. On a school account, an administrator may control installation in workspace settings.


### Are ChatGPT plugins for students free?


The plugin directory does not display prices, and whatever a plugin costs is charged by the vendor rather than by OpenAI, so a ChatGPT subscription buys none of it. Check the vendor's own site before relying on one. Scrimba Explain is free during its open beta, and no other pricing is stated in this article.


### Can Scrimba Explain make flashcards?


No. Scrimba Explain, listed as Explain Video Generator, turns a question, document, webpage or codebase into a narrated explainer video. It produces no flashcards and schedules no reviews. For flashcards from a ChatGPT conversation, Quizlet creates sets from a prompt or a file, and Recall builds spaced repetition decks and schedules them.


## Key Takeaways


- **The comprehension check needs no plugin.** Plain ChatGPT produced three real questions on request, including one that tested transfer rather than recall.
- **An uninstalled plugin fails silently.** Signed out, an at-mention returned ordinary prose with no error, which is why installation comes before evaluation.
- **What those runs prove is narrow.** Signed out versus signed in with the plugin installed shows that installation changes the outcome, and nothing about which plan is required.
- **Review is the job worth an install.** Spaced repetition is scheduling, and Quizlet and Recall do it while the chat cannot.
- **One run each.** The runtimes, slide counts and question quality here are observations from single runs on 8 September 2026, not measurements.
